title: Cryptochromes, Phototropins, and Blue Light
objective: Differentiate major blue-light receptor functions and evaluate blue-light treatments through dose, fraction, background spectrum, and crop response.

terms.definition: Blue/UV-A photoreceptor family involved in photomorphogenesis, circadian regulation, and developmental signaling.
Blue-light receptor family involved in phototropism, stomatal responses, chloroplast movement, and leaf positioning.
Fraction of the defined photon total within a stated blue wavelength band.
Directional growth response to the direction of light.

coreScience: Blue light participates in photosynthesis and also activates multiple receptors. Cryptochrome signaling commonly affects de-etiolation, elongation, circadian regulation, and pigment pathways. Phototropins mediate directional growth, chloroplast movement, leaf positioning, and components of stomatal opening. These networks interact with phytochrome, hormones, temperature, carbon dioxide, and water status.

A blue percentage is incomplete unless the wavelength band, absolute blue photon flux, total PPFD or ePPFD, background spectrum, photoperiod, and measurement method are stated. Ten percent blue at 1,000 PPFD provides twice the blue photon flux of ten percent at 500 PPFD.

Responses are not universally 'compact under blue.' Cannabis morphology and chemical outcomes vary with genotype, intensity, stage, spectral composition, and experimental design. Blue photons may change leaf thickness, area, stomatal behavior, pigmentation, height, and energy efficiency, but these outcomes must be measured rather than inferred from fixture appearance.
cultivationRelevance: Blue-light decisions influence architecture, scouting visibility, human visual comfort, photon efficacy, and possibly transpiration and acclimation.
Spectral trials should compare biologically meaningful photon doses and include leaf temperature, gas exchange or water use, morphology, yield, and quality rather than relying on color descriptions.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Band definition, peak wavelength, absolute blue PFD, blue fraction, total PPFD/ePPFD, and DLI.
Full spectral photon distribution, red/far-red context, photoperiod, and channel timing.
Cultivar, stage, density, prior spectrum, canopy position, and acclimation.
Height, internodes, leaf area and angle, stomatal or water-use data, pigment, biomass, quality, and timing.
Fixture power, photon efficacy, thermal state, and equal-photon or equal-power comparison basis.

misconceptions: Blue light is only for vegetative growth: Blue receptors and photosynthesis function throughout development.
More blue always makes cannabis shorter: Absolute dose, other wavelengths, intensity, genotype, and environment determine response.
A blue-looking lamp has high blue fraction: Human perception cannot quantify spectral photon distribution.
evidenceLimits: Many receptor mechanisms are established across model and horticultural plants, but cannabis production responses are not yet sufficient for one optimal blue fraction.
